key_insight: A convolutional information-theoretic model isolates the vortical flow structures that most causally contribute to a chosen future aerodynamic quantity, such as lift or energy transfer.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted diagnosis of transient gust–airfoil interactions and can help engineers focus on the flow features most responsible for extreme loads and unsteady performance.
method: Decompose each vortical snapshot into informative and residual components using contribution to a future target variable.
Use a convolutional information-theoretic learning framework to identify causally important structures.
Compare extracted structures for different targets, including future lift and scale-dependent energy transfer.
evidence_signal: At Reynolds number 5000, the method highlights vortex cores before impingement and later captures shear layers after massive separation, consistent with the expected evolution of gust-induced loading.
watch_item: The extracted structures depend on the chosen future target and may shift across transient stages, so interpretation requires care when generalizing to other flow conditions or objectives.
paper_title: Extracting informative vortical structures of turbulent wake-extreme vortex gust interactions with machine learning
